thesis: Edgar turns every Vampire cast into a 1/1 from the command zone, free outlets turn those bodies into deaths, death drains bill the table on each one and four gain-to-loss converters bill it again on every gain (three by the amount, Marauding Blight-Priest by the event) - and with the two-card infinite cut for bracket 3, the game ends by accumulation, its one verified finisher a Bloodletter attack (stack 003: seven Sanctum Seeker triggers, each doubled, fourteen a seat).

stages.label: THIRTY-ONE MANA LANDS, SEVEN ROCKS AND A VAMPIRE COST REDUCER
stages.what_it_does: Thirty-two land entries, thirty-five copies (deck-facts: Swamp x4 after v3.0.0 traded Ancient Tomb for a Swamp); thirty-one are here and Phyrexian Tower is filed under conversion because its '{T}, Sacrifice a creature: Add {B}{B}' is a declared free outlet. Seven rocks and Urza's Incubator, which takes up to {2} of GENERIC cost off every Vampire creature spell - the one mana card aimed at the ignition event rather than at mana in general; it takes the full {2} off Edgar himself. The declared ramp component (Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, the three Talismans, the Incubator) is 36.4% of opening sevens and drawn in 77.2% of games, 60.1% by turn six, mean turn 3.49. deck-facts: 12 lands enter tapped; source targets B 36 / R 22 / W 22. Two lands do a second job and stay here because mana is the louder one: Midgar's Reactor Raid sacrifices a creature to draw, Takenuma's channel returns a creature card to hand. Ashnod's Altar and Master of Dark Rites make mana too but only by eating a body, so they are filed where the body goes (conversion, ignition). Master's {B}{B}{B} is spells-only (deck-facts restricted_mana) and cannot pay an activated ability.
cards: Midgar, City of Mako // Reactor Raid

evidence.note: 20 of city-3's 21 (Mana) are here; Phyrexian Tower is filed under conversion
19 of city-0's 20 (Ramp) are here; Ashnod's Altar is in conversion. Exotic Orchard and the rocks share this city with the fetches
8 copies by role (deck-facts), Ashnod's Altar among them

stages.label: A VAMPIRE SPELL IS CAST, AND A BODY APPEARS FROM THE COMMAND ZONE
stages.what_it_does: Nothing starts until a Vampire spell is CAST: eminence makes a 1/1 Vampire from the command zone on every other Vampire cast, so the half the pilot owns is free, undrawable and out of removal's reach, and the half that must be found is the spell. The declared castable-Vampire leg is eight cards: 45.6% of opening sevens, drawn in 86.4% of games, 71.8% by turn six, mean turn 3.03 - the healthiest figure in the brief. Only two of the eight sit here because the other six do a louder second job (Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant and Vraan drain on death; Bloodghast and Charismatic Conqueror are bodies; Cordial Vampire converts deaths into size). Tithe Drinker and Master of Dark Rites are the two whose contribution is the cast: a lifelinker whose extort is a one-point drain on every later spell - and a gain, which a converter turns into a second loss - and a one-drop whose '{T}, Sacrifice another creature: Add {B}{B}{B}' turns a token into the next Vampire spell. Enumerated from cards.json, the 99 holds eleven Vampire creature spells at mana value two or less; the declared leg names eight (proposed edit). Of the 39 creature cards in the 99, six are not Vampires and fire no eminence: Enduring Tenacity, Erebos, Grim Haruspex, Ingris Stingerquill, Midnight Reaper, Morbid Opportunist - two of them (Haruspex, Reaper) arrived in v3.0.0. Edgar on the battlefield is not required for the token, but it is for the free mode of Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat and both modes of Akroma's Will, and stack 003 has him as one of the seven attackers.

evidence.note: Edgar Markov as one of seven attacking Vampires; the four 1/1 Vampire tokens beside him are a given board state, not made in the stack, and its checker records that eminence does not fire there (no spell is cast, hand empty, no mana). For this stage 003 establishes only that Edgar is a Vampire that attacks; the cast-to-token step has no presentable stack on v3.0.0 (open question)
Edgar and Tithe Drinker in city-5 (Card Flow); Master of Dark Rites in city-2 (Finishers); the eight declared castable Vampires spread Finishers 5 / Card Flow 2 / Bodies 1
Master of Dark Rites is the deck's one ramp:dork and deck-facts' one restricted-mana card

stages.label: DRAW WHEN THINGS DIE, AND THREE TUTORS
stages.what_it_does: The pilot's required axis: logged games ran dry by turn eight to ten. The declared draw component is seven cards - 41.2% of opening sevens, drawn in 75.9% of games, 63.6% by turn six, mean turn 3.00 - and v3.0.0 added two draw bodies it does not name (proposed edit). What each reads decides what feeds it. TOKEN deaths draw: Morbid Opportunist (once a turn), Liliana (every creature of yours), Erebos and Crossway Troublemakers (pay 2 life a card; Crossway on Vampires only). NONTOKEN deaths only: Grim Haruspex and Midnight Reaper ('nontoken creature'), so the eminence stream never draws from them - they read a cast body dying, which Bloodghast's landfall return supplies repeatedly, as do Elenda, Tenacity and a sacrificed Vampire spell. ENTRY draws: Welcoming Vampire and Caretaker's Talent fire on the mint itself, once a turn. Clavileno's Demon draws on death; Phyrexian Arena and Twilight Prophet are upkeep draw; Preacher draws on attack while you lead on life - which the converters' gains help keep true. The three tutors are fuel of a different kind: since v3.0.0 there is no two-card line for them to fetch (deck-facts: 0 contained combos), so they are the assisted column of every target - e.g. the drain doubler reads 4.4% assembled and 26.7% assisted. Diabolic Intent is also a death: its additional cost sacrifices a creature, firing every death drain and death draw on the way to the card. Erebos is an outlet and a -2/-1 too; it files here because its draw clause is the static one.

evidence.note: Grim Haruspex, Preacher and Welcoming Vampire in city-5 (Card Flow); Caretaker's Talent, Crossway, Liliana and Erebos in city-1 (Bodies); Clavileno, Morbid Opportunist and Midnight Reaper in city-2 (Finishers); Phyrexian Arena and the three tutors in city-4 (Interaction)
8 copies by role (deck-facts); Midnight Reaper carries only threat:body, so the taxonomy misses its draw
3 copies by role, down from four with Enlightened Tutor cut

stages.label: THE BODIES, THE TWO DOUBLERS, AND KALITAS'S ZOMBIES
stages.what_it_does: What the outlets eat is 1/1 Vampire tokens, and this stage makes more than eminence alone. Two replacement doublers - Anointed Procession and Elspeth, Storm Slayer - apply to every token event: eminence, Charismatic Conqueror's lifelink Vampires, Bloodline Keeper's 2/2 fliers, Preacher's and Clavileno's tokens, Elenda's death payout, Kalitas's Zombies. The declared multiplier component is thin: two cards, 13.7% of opening sevens, drawn in 36.5% of games, 24.7% by turn six (68.2% assisted). The stacks that priced the doubling (002, 010) ran on boards holding Gifted Aetherborn and Mondrak, both cut, and are not presentable, so on v3.0.0 the token count is a claim (open question). Bloodghast returns on every land drop - a nontoken body, so Haruspex and Reaper draw from it. Olivia, Crimson Bride returns a creature card tapped and attacking on each attack, while you control a legendary Vampire. Kalitas (new in v3.0.0) is fodder of a third kind: an opponent's nontoken creature that would die is exiled instead and you get a 2/2 Zombie, so the deck's removal - Olivia's Wrath, Anowon's edict, Liliana's -4, Elspeth's -3, Vish Kal's and Bloodtithe's -X/-X, Olivia Voldaren's ping - mints bodies on your side. The cost: they no longer DIE, so with Kalitas out they fire none of the six cards that read an opponent's death - Blood Artist, Vein Ripper, Cordial Vampire, Elenda, Morbid Opportunist and Yahenni. The Zombie pays it back only when it later dies as yours. The Zombie is not a Vampire: no eminence, no Sanctum Seeker trigger, no Captivating or Lord of Lineage bonus, and it is what Anowon bills you at your upkeep. Kalitas's own '{2}{B}, Sacrifice another Vampire or Zombie' is a mana-gated outlet; it files here because the replacement is the louder job.

evidence.note: Elspeth, Bloodline Keeper, Bloodghast, Olivia Crimson Bride and Kalitas in city-1 (Bodies); Anointed Procession in city-4 (Interaction); Charismatic Conqueror in city-5 (Card Flow)
2 copies by role - the thinnest declared multi-card component
10 copies by role; Kalitas carries it

stages.label: THE OUTLETS, AND THE TWO THAT MAKE A DEATH PAY IN SIZE
stages.what_it_does: The engine proper: a body goes in, a death event comes out, and every death drain and death draw reads that event. The DECLARED free-outlet group is five cards - 31.2% of opening sevens, drawn in 71.6% of games, 54.5% by turn six, mean turn 3.66: Ashnod's Altar ({C}{C} back), Phyrexian Tower ({B}{B} back), Viscera Seer (scry 1), Vish Kal (counters equal to the victim's power, cashed as -1/-1 on a target - the pilot's answer to indestructible, and on the keep list) and Yahenni (indestructible). A sixth no-mana outlet, Master of Dark Rites, is filed under ignition and is not in the group (proposed edit). Mana-gated: Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord ({2}; also gains 1 life per other death - a gain a converter turns into loss) and Anje ({2}, sacrifice a creature or Blood token: each opponent loses 2, you gain 2). Erebos, Kalitas and Diabolic Intent are outlets too, filed under fuel and fodder. Cordial Vampire and Elenda make a death pay in SIZE: Cordial puts a counter on every Vampire per death; Elenda grows per other death and leaves X lifelink tokens when she dies - created, so the doublers apply. No presentable stack names an outlet. Since v3.0.0 this stage is also where the game ends slowly rather than all at once: with no loop to assemble, deaths per turn times drain per death is the clock.

evidence.note: Vish Kal, Yahenni, Edgar Ancient Bloodlord and Anje in city-1 (Bodies); Viscera Seer and Cordial in city-2 (Finishers); Phyrexian Tower in city-3 (Mana); Ashnod's Altar in city-0 (Ramp); Elenda in city-5 (Card Flow) - five cities, the most scattered stage
8 copies by role; Phyrexian Tower, a land, carries none

stages.label: LIFE LOSS WITHOUT COMBAT, AND THE DENIAL SUITE
stages.what_it_does: Two kinds of output. (1) Drains. The declared death drains - Blood Artist (target player, 1, any creature), Cruel Celebrant (each opponent, 1, yours), Vraan (each opponent, 2, once a turn, yours), Vein Ripper (target opponent, 2, any creature; ward - sacrifice a creature) - are 25.8% of opening sevens, drawn in 62.9% of games, 45.3% by turn six, mean turn 3.97. Beside them Sanctum Seeker drains 1 per attacking Vampire, Wispdrinker 1 per small creature entering (every eminence token), Ingris pings per attacker. Every one of these drains except Ingris also GAINS you life, which is what the wincon's converters read. Stack 003 verifies Sanctum Seeker's trigger count: seven attacking Vampires, seven triggers. (2) Removal and denial: Path, Anguished Unmaking (the declared noncreature answer: 7.1% of opening sevens, 21.5% drawn, 59.9% assisted), Olivia's Wrath, Anowon's upkeep edict, Drana and Linvala's lock on creatures' activated abilities, Captivating Vampire's steal, Olivia Voldaren's ping and steal, Bloodtithe Harvester's -X/-X. Olivia's Wrath and Anowon both read 'non-Vampire', and the 99 holds six non-Vampire creatures (enumerated in ignition), plus Kalitas's and Liliana's Zombies and Elspeth's Soldiers: the Wrath's -X/-X hits Grim Haruspex, Midnight Reaper, Morbid Opportunist and Ingris on your own side, and Tenacity returns as an enchantment. Each of those is also a death event for the drains.

evidence.note: Sanctum Seeker: one trigger per attacking Vampire, 1 per opponent each before Bloodletter doubles it

Blood Artist, Cruel Celebrant, Vraan, Sanctum Seeker, Anowon and Bloodtithe Harvester in city-2 (Finishers); Vein Ripper, Ingris, Drana and Linvala, Captivating and Olivia Voldaren in city-1 (Bodies); Path, Anguished Unmaking and Olivia's Wrath in city-4 (Interaction); Wispdrinker in city-5 (Card Flow)

stages.label: FOUR HELD, THREE OF THEM FREE OR DOUBLED WITH EDGAR OUT
stages.what_it_does: Held, not cast. Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are free 'if you control a commander', and Akroma's Will takes both modes under the same condition - so Edgar on the battlefield, not in the command zone, is what makes this suite cheap. The component is 25.8% of opening sevens, drawn in 62.5% of games, 45.3% by turn six, mean turn 3.97. What each reaches: Flawless Maneuver and Akroma's Will name CREATURES, so they cover Vito, Bloodletter and the drain bodies but never Sanguine Bond or Anointed Procession; Teferi's Protection phases out every permanent and is the only one of the four that answers an exile, bounce or -X/-X sweeper; Deflecting Swat retargets one targeted spell or ability of any kind. Akroma's Will's lifelink mode is also offence: every creature you control gains life on damage, which a converter in wincon turns into loss. Self-protection filed elsewhere: Enduring Tenacity's death-return (it comes back as an enchantment with its drain intact - stack 012 established the return clause on a board that also held the cut Conqueror, and is cited here for that clause only), Vein Ripper's ward, Yahenni's and Erebos's indestructible. This is the stage the map agrees with completely: all four sit together in city-6, because protection is what the card SAYS.

evidence.note: all four in city-6 (Insurance), a city that is this stage and nothing else

stages.label: FOUR CONVERTERS AND ONE DOUBLER, FINITE NOW
stages.what_it_does: v3.0.0 cut both loss-to-gain halves (Bloodthirsty Conqueror, Exquisite Blood) for bracket 3, and deck-facts now reads 0 contained combo lines and 0 two-card infinites. The game no longer ends when two cards meet; it ends by accumulation, and these five cards are what multiply it. CONVERTERS: Vito, Sanguine Bond and Enduring Tenacity read 'whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life' - amount-scaled, aimed at one seat; Marauding Blight-Priest reads 'each opponent loses 1 life' per gain event - count-scaled, table-wide. They are the declared gain-to-loss component, 25.8% of opening sevens (32.1% by turn three), and they now loop with nothing: each turns a gain from output (every death drain but Ingris gains), from lifelink (Tithe Drinker, Kalitas, Vish Kal, Elenda's tokens, Crossway's attackers, Akroma's Will, Vito's own {3}{B}{B} activation) or from Anje and Edgar, Ancient Bloodlord into a second loss. The declared converter target measures one drawn in 61.8% of games (81.0% assisted), 44.5% by turn six, mean turn 4.03. DOUBLER: Bloodletter of Aclazotz doubles every opponent's loss on your turn. Stack 003 is the one fact-tier kill on this list: seven attacking Vampires through Sanctum Seeker drain 14 a seat before blockers. Its declared component is Bloodletter plus Sanctum Seeker, 4.4% assembled (26.7% assisted, mean turn 6.91), and deck-audit prices Bloodletter as a one-card point of failure at 7.1% of opening sevens - of that route, not of this stage: without it the four converters still end the game by accumulation, only slower and unverified. Whether Bloodletter also doubles a converter's loss on your turn is a reading until a stack runs it.
cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

evidence.note: Bloodletter doubles each opponent's loss per Sanctum Seeker trigger on your turn: 7 x 2 = 14 per seat; your own gain is not doubled. 003 shows the doubling for Sanctum Seeker's triggers only; every card on its board is in v3.0.0 (Edgar as commander)
Tenacity and Blight-Priest in city-2 (Finishers); Vito and Bloodletter in city-1 (Bodies); Sanguine Bond in city-4 (Interaction)

via: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose
lines.note: READING. Attacking Vampires gain lifelink, so a connecting attack's damage comes back as Vito's 'that much' aimed at one seat. Whether simultaneous lifelink damage from several attackers is one gain event or one per source sets the Blight-Priest count - open question.
READING. A free outlet turns any body, eminence token included, into a death event, which every death drain reads. No presentable stack names an outlet.

READING. Anowon's upkeep edict on an opponent's nontoken non-Vampire is exiled by Kalitas and becomes your 2/2 Zombie; at your next upkeep that Zombie is a non-Vampire you can give to Anowon - a death event for the drains. Needs a stack.

READING. One Vampire cast, one eminence event, two replacement doublers: 1 -> 2 -> 4 tokens. Stacks 002 and 010 proved the shape on boards holding cut cards and are not presentable; on v3.0.0 the count is a claim.
READING. The eminence token is a token with power 2 or less, so each mint is a Welcoming Vampire card and a Caretaker's Talent card, each once a turn.
READING. Wispdrinker drains 1 per other small creature entering, so the mint bills the table before anything dies - and gains, which a converter reads.
READING. The Incubator reduces generic cost only, up to {2}: Edgar's {3}{R}{W}{B} becomes {1}{R}{W}{B}; on the one-drops and the {B}{B} and {W}{B} two-drops it saves nothing.

map_disagreements.why: A converter is one sentence - 'whenever you gain life, target opponent loses that much life' - printed on a legendary creature (Vito, Bodies), an enchantment creature and a Cleric (Tenacity and Blight-Priest, Finishers) and a five-mana enchantment that the map files with the tutors and removal (Sanguine Bond, Interaction). The map reads card type and surrounding text; the job is the one shared sentence, which it cannot see. With the loss-to-gain halves cut, nothing on the map marks this group as the deck's finisher at all.

An outlet is defined by a cost - 'Sacrifice a creature:' - printed on a land (Phyrexian Tower, Mana), an artifact that reads as a rock (Ashnod's Altar, Ramp), a one-drop Vampire (Viscera Seer, Finishers) and two legendary bodies (Vish Kal, Yahenni, Bodies). The shared job is invisible to the embedding; the conversion stage spans five cities.

map_disagreements.component: A castable Vampire drawn (the ignition leg)
map_disagreements.why: Ignition is a property of the type line and the mana value - Vampire, two or less - and the map reads through the ability text, so the eight declared casts sort by what they do after they resolve. The engine's first event has no city.

The map sorts draw by its trigger event and card type: death-draw bodies (Morbid Opportunist, Midnight Reaper) file with the death drains in Finishers, entry-draw (Welcoming Vampire) and Grim Haruspex in Card Flow, the planeswalker and the Class with the big bodies, Phyrexian Arena with the tutors. A correct reading of text, the wrong reading of the stage - and the token/nontoken split that decides what feeds each one is not visible in either.

map_disagreements.component: A token multiplier or extra token-maker drawn
map_disagreements.why: Anointed Procession is a white enchantment and clusters with the enchantment-and-instant answers; Elspeth is a planeswalker that makes bodies. Both carry the same replacement sentence, which is the whole job here.
Full agreement, recorded as the control case: the four instants say what they do and nothing else. Where the map and the engine agree it is because the card's text IS its job.

critic.summary: Round one on the v3.0.0 model. Two fail grounds. (1) lines[0] (ignition -> wincon via Edgar Markov) cites stack 003, but nothing in 003 is ignition: no spell is cast, eminence never triggers (the checker's own summary: 'no other triggers exist in the scenario (Eminence needs a cast...)'), and Edgar's one trigger is established in step 3 to change nothing about the drain. Edgar contributes only one attacking Vampire body; the 'four eminence tokens' are a scenario premise with no provenance. Solid green for a flow the stack shows not happening. lines[1] (Sanctum Seeker -> Bloodletter, same stack) is the honest version and stands. (2) The wincon stage says the converters' declared target 'still names the cut halves and reads 0.0 by construction (proposed edit)'; goldfish_targets.json now declares 'A life-gain-to-loss converter drawn' with exactly the four converters, and goldfish_metrics.json (sha 1df3a335..., matching decklist.txt) measures it at 61.8% assembled / 81.0% assisted / 44.5% by turn six. open_questions[4] and proposed_goldfish_edits[0] carry the same stale premise. Everything else re-derived: every component figure, every role count, every city membership, the 39/6/11 creature enumerations, the six no-mana outlets, the 97 placements; eight dashed lines are labelled READING and none outruns its oracle text; all eight what_it_does are under 1,600 characters.

findings.claim: from ignition to wincon via Edgar Markov, Sanctum Seeker, Bloodletter; verified_by 003: 'Seven attacking Vampires (Edgar and four eminence tokens among them) give seven Sanctum Seeker triggers ... The only verified kill on v3.0.0'
findings.note: The ignition stage's resource is 'A VAMPIRE SPELL IS CAST, AND A BODY APPEARS FROM THE COMMAND ZONE'. Stack 003 casts nothing: scenario.hand is [], mana_available is '', the board lists 'four 1/1 black Vampire creature tokens' with no provenance, and the checker's summary states 'no other triggers exist in the scenario (Eminence needs a cast; opponents' boards are empty)'. So the stack establishes that eminence does NOT occur on this board. Edgar's only ability that resolves is his attack trigger, and resolution step 3 establishes that it 'do[es] NOT change the trigger drain at all'. Edgar's whole contribution to the 14 is being the seventh attacking Vampire (one Sanctum Seeker trigger) - a body any Vampire supplies, not an ignition event. The arrow is the stack's cards named, not its flow supported. What 003 does carry is already lines[1]. To survive: drop verified_by (dash it as a READING that eminence casts supply the attackers), or re-run a stack that casts a Vampire with Edgar in the command zone and then attacks. 'Every card on the board is still in the 99' is also loose: Edgar is the commander, not in the 99. Not cleanly mechanizable (the same wrong line survives a rephrase); a weak check would flag a verified line whose stack's checker summary names one of the line's via cards' abilities as not occurring.

findings.claim: Stack 003: 'Edgar on the battlefield as one of seven attacking Vampires beside four eminence tokens'
findings.note: Same defect as lines[0], smaller. The tokens in 003 are a given board state; the stack does not make them, and its checker says eminence does not fire there. 'beside four 1/1 Vampire tokens' is what 003 supports. As evidence for the ignition stage, 003 establishes only that Edgar is a Vampire that attacks.

findings.claim: four gain-to-loss converters bill it again for every point gained ... its one verified finisher a Bloodletter turn that doubles every drain (stack 003: fourteen a seat from seven attackers)
findings.note: Two small things, neither a fail ground alone. 'For every point gained' is true of three converters; Marauding Blight-Priest reads 'Whenever you gain life, each opponent loses 1 life' - per event, as stages[7] itself says (count-scaled). And 003 establishes doubling for Sanctum Seeker's triggers only; stages[7] and open_questions[0] correctly call Bloodletter on a converter's loss 'a reading until a stack runs it', while the thesis states 'doubles every drain' beside a 003 citation. Bloodletter's oracle does cover any opponent loss on your turn, so the claim is likely true - but the citation in the parenthesis does not carry 'every'. The 14-a-seat figure is supported.

Enumerated from cards.json: Bloodletter is the only card that doubles life loss, so for THE DRAIN DOUBLER route it is one card (deck-audit: 7.1% of opening sevens, 26.7% assisted). But the stage is labelled 'FOUR CONVERTERS AND ONE DOUBLER' and its own prose says the game now ends by accumulation through the converters, which are a four-card component measured at 61.8% assembled. Losing Bloodletter costs the stage its only verified route, not the stage. This reads the audit's one-card class as the stage's failure point. Either scope it (the SPOF of the verified finisher, which is true) or rebut by defining the stage as that route. Contrast stages[5], where the audit's other one-card SPOF (Anguished Unmaking - confirmed the only nonland-permanent exile in the 99) is correctly NOT promoted because the stage has other jobs.

findings.claim: Kalitas ... so the deck's removal - Olivia's Wrath, Anowon's edict, Liliana's -4, Elspeth's -3, Vish Kal's and Bloodtithe's -X/-X, Olivia Voldaren's ping - mints bodies on your side
findings.note: The replacement is read correctly (oracle: 'If a nontoken creature an opponent controls would die, instead exile that card and create a 2/2 black Zombie'), but it is filed as pure gain. The same replacement means those creatures never DIE, so with Kalitas out an opponent's nontoken creature is no longer a death event for Blood Artist and Vein Ripper ('a creature dies'), Cordial Vampire and Elenda ('another creature dies') or Yahenni ('a creature an opponent controls dies'). Each Zombie is one later death of your own; each exile removes up to five triggers now, Vein Ripper's worth 2. The fodder -> output flow the model draws through Kalitas has a cost in output it does not state. Not a fail ground: no sentence is false, but a stage that argues Kalitas is fodder should price both sides. Also relevant to the goldfish: meta.death_rate.opponent_per_turn 1.31 comes from a 2026-10-01 Forge run on a pre-Kalitas list.

findings.claim: READING. Anowon's upkeep edict on an opponent's nontoken non-Vampire is exiled by Kalitas and becomes your 2/2 Zombie; at your next upkeep that Zombie is a non-Vampire you can give to Anowon - a death event for the drains. Needs a stack.
findings.note: Dashed, labelled, and the reading follows the oracle (sacrifice is a 'die' event, so Kalitas replaces it). open_questions[3] asks the right question. The Zombie's later death is a death event for Blood Artist and Cruel Celebrant; note that the opponent's creature itself, being exiled, is not (see stages[3]).
